target: A developer in India, 18 to 34, who is early in the job, switching into it, or still trying to get the first role, and who wants to understand systems by doing the work rather than watching a lesson

behaviours.name: Free-first
behaviours.how: Uses free labs, YouTube, and public university courses, and pays only when the free version stops.

behaviours.name: Cert hunter
behaviours.how: Pays for a browser lab when a job posting or a certificate names the tool.

behaviours.name: Interview prep
behaviours.how: Spends on DSA and system-design prep because that is what the interview asks.

behaviours.name: Deal hunter
behaviours.how: Waits for a sale, a student price, or an annual discount before paying.

behaviours.name: Reads every review
behaviours.how: Checks Reddit and review sites, and remembers labs that crashed or products that stopped shipping.

behaviours.name: Builds on their own machine
behaviours.how: Clones a free course and runs it locally rather than pay for a browser.

behaviours.name: Employer pays
behaviours.how: Will expense a tool if a manager agrees, and will not buy it from a stipend.

objections: I can do the MIT labs and Mini-LSM for free.
A browser lab I already know is free, or about $6 a month.
Last time I paid for labs, they crashed and I lost the hour.
This will not get me hired. Interviews ask DSA and system design.
I need Kubernetes on my resume, not an LSM tree.
I still have to do the hard work, and the lesson may stop explaining.
If I pay for a year, they might stop building it.
A few hundred rupees a month per track adds up, and I might not finish.
habits: you study at night after college or after work, on a laptop
you already have a YouTube systems video half-finished
you are applying to SDE or DevOps roles in the next few months
you will not open a cloud account of your own
the money you can spend is a stipend, a first salary, or what your family allows
